correctness.rationale: For all positive rates and times, direct generator exponentiation is convolution with the difference-of-Poisson Skellam mass. Turán/log-concavity and telescoping give the exact twice-mode total variation norm, attained by sign inputs. The Riccati comparison proves the strict increase in time of each adjacent Bessel mass ratio; Turán proves its decrease with index, yielding unique ordered thresholds and no skipped/tied nonadjacent modes. Analytic differentiation gives a positive, explicit one-sided slope jump. Gaussian Fourier expansion with exponentially controlled tails and odd-moment cancellation gives the \(O(k^{-1})\) two-term time shift. Assumptions, sign, index boundaries and fixed-drift limitation are explicit. Two hundred forty finite checker assertions were run but are not treated as proofs of infinite behavior.

originality.rationale: The Skellam representation, modified-Bessel inequalities and generic heat-smoothing techniques are prior material, not claimed new. The inspected mathematical conclusions give probability masses, bounds, or statistical modeling, not the exact asymmetric heat-gradient operator norm together with its infinite ordered temporal corners, positive jumps and index-dependent location expansion. Published mathematical-record searches and recoverable related claims were compared by implication. The record supports best-knowledge originality, not a proof of absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: The exact norm determines the worst bounded input amplification by the spatial derivative of a nonreversible lattice heat semigroup. The infinite ordered sharp modal transitions, their strictly positive derivative cusps, exact special symmetric analytic regime and shifted time asymptotic quantify a robust, naturally motivated nonsmoothness phenomenon not captured by generic heat-gradient decay or probability point-mass bounds. This is a structural characterization, not a numerical table or parameter relabeling.
